# crossmet

**crossmet** provides tools for importing, summarising and visualising
daily meteorological observations from the AFBI Crossnacreevy weather
station in Northern Ireland.

The package reads annual worksheets from an Excel workbook, reshapes the
observations into a tidy long-format data frame, produces year-specific
monthly summaries and long-term monthly climate summaries, and creates
weather plots.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

\`\`\`r install.packages(“pak”) pak::pak(“GABurns/crossmet”) \`\`\`

## Import weather observations

\`ImportWeather()\` reads the worksheets needed for the requested date
range. Worksheets are expected to be named with their four-digit year
(for example, \`2023\`) and to follow the Crossnacreevy workbook layout.

\`\`\`r library(crossmet)

weather \<- ImportWeather( file = “data/crossnacreevy_weather.xlsx”,
start_date = “2020-01-01”, end_date = “2024-12-31” )

head(weather) \`\`\`

The returned data frame contains \`Date\`, \`DOY\`, \`variable\` and
\`value\` columns, with one row per date and weather variable.

## Monthly summaries

\`MonthlySummaryTable()\` calculates monthly values separately for each
year. Rainfall and daily solar-radiation totals are summed; daily
maximum temperature is represented by its monthly maximum; daily minimum
temperature by its monthly minimum; and other variables by their monthly
mean.

\`\`\`r yearly_months \<- MonthlySummaryTable(weather) \`\`\`

\`ClimateSummaryTable()\` calculates long-term monthly climatological
values. It first calculates the relevant monthly statistic for each
year, then averages those yearly monthly values across the available
years. This means rainfall climatology is the mean of annual monthly
rainfall totals, rather than the average daily rainfall.

\`\`\`r climate_normals \<- ClimateSummaryTable(weather) \`\`\`

Missing observations are excluded from calculations. A yearly monthly
statistic is \`NA\` when that group has no observed values; a
climatological average is \`NA\` when all years are missing for that
month and variable.

## Visualise weather data

The plotting functions return ggplot objects and can be customised with
normal ggplot2 layers.

\`\`\`r PlotMonthlyGrid(weather, variable = “RH (%)”)
RainfallPlot(weather) TemperaturePlot(weather) \`\`\`

To save a selection of plots and the monthly grid plots:

\`\`\`r saved_files \<- SaveWeatherPlots( weather, plots =
c(“temperature”, “rainfall”, “relative_humidity”), monthly_grids = TRUE,
path = “outputs/weather-plots” )

saved_files \`\`\`

The function returns the paths of all files it creates, including
monthly grid images.

## Input workbook requirements

- Each worksheet represents one calendar year and is named using that
  year.
- The workbook contains two header rows followed by daily observations.
- The expected weather columns are Date, DOY, minimum and maximum
  temperature, mean air temperature, temperature difference, rainfall,
  soil temperatures, average wind speed, relative humidity, leaf wetness
  and daily solar radiation.
- Date values must be readable by readxl as Excel dates.

See the function help pages for complete argument details:

\`\`\`r ?ImportWeather ?MonthlySummaryTable ?ClimateSummaryTable
?PlotMonthlyGrid ?SaveWeatherPlots \`\`\`

## Development

Run the package tests with:

\`\`\`r pak::pak(“GABurns/crossmet”) testthat::test_local() \`\`\`

The package uses testthat edition 3.

# Package index

## Data preparation

Functions for importing and preparing daily weather data.

- [`ImportWeather()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/ImportWeather.md)
  : Import weather data from Excel

## Monthly summaries

Functions for calculating monthly weather statistics.

- [`ClimateSummaryTable()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/ClimateSummaryTable.md)
  : Monthly Climate Summary Table
- [`MonthlySummaryTable()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/MonthlySummaryTable.md)
  : Monthly Summary Table

## Visualisations

Functions for creating weather data plots.

- [`LeafWetnessPlot()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/LeafWetnessPlot.md)
  : Plot leaf wetness
- [`MeanAirTempPlot()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/MeanAirTempPlot.md)
  : Plot mean air temperature
- [`RainfallPlot()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/RainfallPlot.md)
  : title Plot daily rainfall
- [`RelativeHumidityPlot()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/RelativeHumidityPlot.md)
  : Plot relative humidity
- [`SoilTempPlot()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/SoilTempPlot.md)
  : Plot soil temperature
- [`SolarRadPlot()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/SolarRadPlot.md)
  : Plot daily light totals
- [`TemperatureDifferencePlot()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/TemperatureDifferencePlot.md)
  : Plot temperature difference
- [`TemperaturePlot()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/TemperaturePlot.md)
  : Plot minimum and maximum air temperature
- [`WindSpeedPlot()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/WindSpeedPlot.md)
  : Plot average wind speed
- [`PlotMonthlyGrid()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/PlotMonthlyGrid.md)
  : PlotMonthlyGrid

## Utiltity

Misc. Functions

- [`SaveWeatherPlots()`](https://GABurns.github.io/crossmet/reference/SaveWeatherPlots.md)
  : Save weather plots
